key_insight: Sequential sharing reproduces all two-observer parallel statistics and can sustain quantum advantage for arbitrarily more observers in certain tasks, while parallel sharing becomes useful in specific constrained tasks.
engineering_relevance: Quantum communication networks should choose sequential reuse or parallel distribution according to the task, since these architectures can support very different numbers of advantaged observers.
method: Compare statistics achievable through sequential and parallel information sharing.
Analyze quantum-advantage sharing in tasks with two decoding measurements.
Contrast parallel sharing in 3-bit random access codes (RACs) and parity-oblivious RACs.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports theoretical results: two-observer statistical equivalence in one direction, an arbitrarily large sequential–parallel sustainability gap, and parallel advantage for at most two observers in a 3-bit parity-oblivious RAC using imperfect clones.
watch_item: The conclusions are task-dependent, and the abstract does not report experimental validation or robustness to implementation noise.
paper_title: Sequential vs parallel Strategies for Sharing Quantum Advantage in Communication Tasks
